taxonomy:
Below is a taxonomy for **grid-based logic games**, organized by **core solving object/mechanism** (how the player’s actions relate to the final configuration). Each listed game is placed under the most fitting category.

---

## 1) Constraint on **placing/colouring cells**
Games where the key decision is to paint/shade certain cells (black/white/coloured) subject to adjacency/area/shape constraints.

- **Akari** (light bulbs vs black squares; illumination constraints)
- **Choco Banana** (paint cells black with rectangle/square linkage rules)
- **Heyawake** (painted cells separated; room counts)
- **Hitori** (black/white cell colouring)
- **Kurodoko** (black/white cell colouring with distance-to-black-number rules)
- **Kurotto** (colouring cells using circles as clues)
- **LITS** (colour tetromino cells in regions)
- **Nurikabe** (black wall / white area rules)
- **Nurimeizu** (two blocks of same size/number per region; shaded cells)
- **Nurimisaki** (white misaki cells; black/white connectivity)
- **Nuritwin** (two connected shaded blocks per region; connectivity/separation rules)
- **Sto-stone** (drop “stones” / resulting black-cell pattern constraints)
- **Tilepaint** (colour tiles into final shape)
- **Usowan** (coloured cells adjacent-number rule, plus wrong-number per bold-rectangle)
- **Yajilin** (loop avoids numbers/black cells; but also implies forbidden black-cell set given by puzzle)
  - *Placed here because it crucially depends on the given “black cells” and number-cells rather than the loop alone.*

---

## 2) Constraint on **placing geometric shapes in cells/regions**
Games where the main objects are blocks/shapes/rectangles/tilings/tetrominoes.

- **Chained Block** (blocks of consecutive black cells; chain through corners; uniqueness by shape)
- **Double Choco** (pair of same-form areas; block tiling by dotted/solid lines)
- **Evolomino** (blocks of identical size filled/duplicated under arrow routes)
- **Five Cells** (partition into blocks of exactly 5)
- **Fillomino** (fill blocks by numbers; each block size matches)
- **Hashiwokakero** (bridge graph between islands; involves connectivity but not colouring)
- **Hebi** (snake-like numbered path in cells)
- **LITS** (tetrominoes per region)
- **Shakashaka** (triangles in squares leaving uncovered rectangle/square)
- **Shikaku** (partition grid into rectangles by numbers)
- **Sashigane** (L-shaped blocks with knee/arrow/open-circle constraints)

---

## 3) **Loop / path games** (single non-self-crossing loop)
Games where you draw one or more loop(s) through grid cell-centers or along dot edges, with “must pass through” and “turn/straight” constraints.

- **Dotchi-Loop** (single loop through white circles; no black circles)
- **Masyu** (loop with black/white circle turn/straight rules)
- **Mid-loop** (loop passing through black circles at segment midpoint)
- **Moon-or-Sun** (loop visits each room once; all moons or all suns per room; alternation between rooms)
- **Nagareru** (directional wind constrains loop movement)
- **Suraromu** (loop through gates; gates only once; start/end at numbered open circle)
- **Slitherlink** (loop around cells with numeric edge counts)
- **Yajilin** (single loop; forbidden black cells and number-cells; black cells can’t touch)

---

## 4) **Connectivity/flow with graph-like line drawing**
Games where lines connect specific items (pairs, islands, or digits) forming networks (often without crossing/branching).

- **Hashiwokakero** (islands connected by 1–2 bridges; bridges make continuous link)
- **Numberlink** (connect pairs of equal numbers with a continuous non-crossing line)
- **Satogaeri** (move circles per country until each country has exactly one; circles can’t cross each other’s tracks)
- **Ripple Effect** (rooms filled with consecutive numbers; not line-drawing, but constraint akin to “propagation” across rows/cols inside regions)
- **Norinori** (place blocks in pairs in consecutive black squares)
  - *Included here conceptually as a paired placement that behaves like constrained connectivity.*

---

## 5) **Directional / motion / “route” games**
Games where arrows, direction, or movement rules define how the solution advances (often still inside a grid, sometimes not a loop).

- **Hebi** (snakes with direction-of-view attack constraints; numbered black squares)
- **Nagareru** (loop as wind-blown directed motion)
- **Pencils** (draw pencil lines from tip following length digits)
- **Sashigane** (arrows point to the knee—directional within an L-block)
- **Satogaeri** (circles move along tracks; distance constraints from circle numbers)
- **Yosenabe** (circles move into grey regions; arrows show motion direction; sums match per region)

---

## 6) **Tessellation / partitioning of regions with local rules (non-loop)**
Games where the board is partitioned (rectangles/rooms/regions/blocks), and each region obeys internal arithmetic or adjacency constraints.

- **Nurimeizu** (rooms/outlined regions each contain exactly two blocks of same number)
- **Heyawake** (bold-line rooms with painted-cell counts)
- **Juosan** (bold-line territories and placing — or | symbols)
- **Ripple Effect** (rooms with consecutive numbering starting from 1)
- **Kurodoko** (numbers constrain nearest black in row/column; though it’s not a pure partitioner, it still behaves as a region-like constraint)
- **Nurikabe** (white areas partitioned by black walls; each white area has one number)
- **Suraromu** (gates and loop over grid; still region/feature based)

---

## 7) **Classic exact-cover / Sudoku-style constraints**
Games defined by row/column/block uniqueness constraints.

- **Sudoku** (1–9 in each row/column/3×3 block)

---

## Full game list placed into the taxonomy (by category)
- **Constraint on placing/colouring cells:**  
  Akari, Choco Banana, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, LITS, Nurikabe, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Yajilin
- **Geometric shapes/tilings/blocks:**  
  Chained Block, Double Choco, Evolomino, Five Cells, Fillomino, LITS, Shakashaka, Shikaku, Sashigane
- **Single loop games:**  
  Dotchi-Loop, Masyu, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu, Slitherlink, Yajilin
- **Connectivity/graph line games:**  
  Hashiwokakero, Numberlink
- **Directional/motion/path without classic loop:**  
  Hebi, Nagareru, Pencils, Sashigane, Satogaeri, Yosenabe
- **Partitioning into regions with local rules:**  
  Juosan, Ripple Effect, Nurikabe, Heyawake, Nurimeizu, (also overlaps with several above)
- **Sudoku-style:**  
  Sudoku

---

If you want, I can also:
1) re-tune the taxonomy so every game appears **exactly once** (no overlaps), or  
2) output this as a **JSON/YAML** structure for easier reuse.
